When making a device available on the market, distributors must act with due care and verify that: (a) the device is CE marked and the EU declaration of conformity is drawn up; (b) the device is accompanied by the required manufacturer information under Article 10(11); (c) the importer has met the requirements of Article 13(3) for imported devices; and (d) a UDI is assigned where applicable (which may be verified via representative sampling).

If a distributor has reason to believe a device is non-compliant, it must withhold the device from the market, inform the manufacturer, authorised representative (if applicable), and importer, and additionally inform the competent authority if the device presents a serious risk or is falsified.

Distributors must also ensure that storage and transport conditions meet the manufacturer's specifications while under their responsibility, immediately inform supply chain partners and cooperate with authorities if a distributed device is found non-compliant, and avoid actions under Article 16—such as marketing under their own name, altering the intended purpose, or modifying the device—that would transfer manufacturer obligations to them.
Manufacturers of custom-made devices must draw up, keep up to date, and keep available for competent authorities documentation in accordance with Section 2 of Annex XIII (Article 10(5)).
Under Article 21(1) and Article 10(6), custom-made devices must not bear the CE marking, and the requirement to draw up an EU declaration of conformity under Article 10(6) does not apply.

In accordance with Article 21(1)(b) and 21(2), custom-made devices may be made available on the market if Article 52(8) and Annex XIII are complied with, and they must be accompanied by the statement referred to in Section 1 of Annex XIII, made available to the particular patient or user identified by name, acronym, or numerical code.
Additionally, manufacturers must submit a list of such devices made available in their territory if required by Member States.

Pursuant to Article 52(3), manufacturers of class III devices, other than custom-made or investigational devices, must undergo a conformity assessment as specified in Annex IX, or alternatively, a conformity assessment as specified in Annex X coupled with Annex XI.

For class III custom-made implantable devices, manufacturers must follow Annex XIII and additionally undergo conformity assessment specified in Chapter I of Annex IX or Part A of Annex XI as per Article 52(8).
Specific additional procedures in Annex IX or Annex X may also apply under Article 52(9)-(11) depending on device characteristics.

Under the General Safety and Performance Requirements, manufacturers must establish, implement, document, and maintain a risk management system as a continuous iterative process throughout the entire device lifecycle that requires regular systematic updating.

In carrying out this system, manufacturers must: (a) establish and document a risk management plan for each device; (b) identify and analyse known and foreseeable hazards; (c) estimate and evaluate risks occurring during intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse; (d) eliminate or control these risks in accordance with specified safety principles and priority order; (e) evaluate the impact of information from production and post-market surveillance on hazards, frequencies, risk estimates, overall risk, benefit-risk ratio, and risk acceptability; and (f) amend control measures as necessary based on that evaluation.
